title: Regional trade agreements and the WTO

stages.name: Regional trade agreements and the WTO
stages.title: Regional trade agreements and the WTO
stages.sub: How regional deals can both help and hurt trade, and where they clash with WTO rules.

steps.q: Before a customs union forms, a country buys wheat from a cheap outside seller because no one inside the bloc can match that price. After the union removes internal tariffs, a member country can now sell wheat almost as cheaply, tariff-free. If this member can genuinely match costs once tariffs are stripped away, who ends up supplying the wheat?
steps.right: The member country, at a lower price than before
steps.wrong: The same outside seller, since they were cheapest before
steps.hint: Removing tariffs between members can reveal who is truly cheapest once trade barriers are gone.

steps.q: So buyers switch to this low-cost member, tariffs fall, prices fall, and consumers who could not afford wheat before now buy it. What happens to the total amount of trade taking place?
steps.hint: New buyers are drawn in by the lower price, on top of the buyers who already existed.

steps.q: Now picture a different case. Before the union, a country bought machinery from the cheapest seller in the world, outside the bloc. After joining the union, that outside seller still faces a tariff, but a member country's machinery is tariff-free even though it costs more to actually produce. Which supplier does the buyer now switch to?
steps.right: The costlier member producer, because it is tariff-free
steps.wrong: The original cheapest outside seller, since it stays cheapest
steps.hint: The tariff, not the true production cost, now decides who looks cheaper.

steps.right: Less efficiently, output shifts to a costlier producer
steps.wrong: More efficiently, since the internal price fell

steps.q: The WTO's core rule says a country must offer the same low tariff to every trading partner equally, with no favourites. A customs union instead gives its own members zero tariffs while keeping tariffs on everyone else outside the bloc. Does the union's special treatment of its own members fit that equal-treatment rule?
steps.right: No, it treats outsiders worse than members
steps.wrong: Yes, because tariffs are still positive for outsiders
steps.hint: Equal treatment means no partner gets favoured over another; a bloc's members are favoured by definition.

steps.q: Regional trade agreements are allowed under WTO rules as an exception, yet they deliberately favour insiders over outsiders and can divert trade to costlier producers. Does this sit comfortably alongside the WTO's aim of equal, worldwide trade liberalisation?
steps.right: No, the two aims can pull against each other
steps.wrong: Yes, they always work smoothly together
steps.hint: One system favours a select group, the other insists on equal treatment for all.
